Sepsis-3 cohorts across sources

Source: vignettes/sepsis-cohort-definitions.Rmd
sepsis-cohort-definitions.Rmd

Sepsis-3 is a clinical definition, not an ICD code. rendehR ships one implementation per source family so the same rule runs on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and eICU, with the source-specific tables and item IDs each database needs.

The definition

The Third International Consensus defines sepsis as suspected infection co-occurring with an acute increase in organ dysfunction, measured by the SOFA score. There is no gold-standard way to find it in ICU records: published studies differ in how they detect suspected infection, how they measure the SOFA increase, which time window they use and what they count. rendehR ships a default and keeps the alternatives as options, so the choice is explicit.

Default (definition = "delta"). It follows the YAIB/ricu operationalisation:

  1. Suspected infection. On MIMIC, an antibiotic paired with a body-fluid culture: if the culture came first, the antibiotic must follow within 72 hours; if the antibiotic came first, the culture must follow within 24 hours. The earlier event is the suspicion time. eICU has culture data for under 3% of stays, so there the antibiotic alone is the suspicion (as in ricu and YAIB). In both, the antibiotic must belong to a course lasting at least 72 hours (administrations less than 24 hours apart form one course), or a course cut short by death.
  2. SOFA rise. The hourly 24-hour SOFA minus the lowest SOFA of the stay so far must reach 2 points. Organ dysfunction present from ICU admission (an injury, sedation, a vasopressor started on arrival) is the baseline, not sepsis. This matters for trauma and spinal cord injury patients.
  3. Combination. Keep ICU stays where such a rise falls within −48 to +24 hours of the suspicion time. Adults only.

definition = "absolute". The earlier rendehR rule: any antibiotic (MIMIC-III and eICU) or antibiotic-culture pair (MIMIC-IV), and an absolute SOFA of at least 2 from an assumed baseline of 0. It is the rule of the AI Clinician code (microsoft/mimic_sepsis) and MIMIC-Sepsis, and it selects many more stays.

bundle = "trauma_sepsis3" (MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV). Hospital-acquired sepsis in trauma admissions, after SepsisOnset_TraumaCohort: a blood culture at least 72 hours after admission with a new intravenous antibiotic course of at least 4 days starting within 2 days of it, and a rise of at least 2 points of a SOFA without its GCS and urine-output parts within 3 days of the culture. It is decided per hospital admission; eICU lacks the culture data it needs.

The definitions were compared with these published operationalisations: YAIB (used by Tranchellini et al., npj Digit Med 2026 and its code), microsoft/mimic_sepsis, MIMIC-Sepsis, SepsisOnset_TraumaCohort and Zhang et al., npj Digit Med 2026.

Using the helper 

ehr_init_project(
  "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "sepsis-demo",
  raw_data_root = normalizePath("rendehr-demo/data/source_data")
)

build_sepsis_cohort() runs the packaged SQL and returns the selected identifiers. With import = FALSE it writes only a CSV, so you can inspect the cohort before committing it to a project:

out <- file.path(docs_root, "sepsis-demo/mimic_iv_demo_sepsis3.csv")
build_sepsis_cohort(
  "mimic_iv_demo", bundle = "sepsis3",
  import = FALSE, out_csv = out, show_progress = FALSE
)
ids <- read.csv(out)
nrow(ids)
#> [1] 39
length(unique(ids$subject_id))
#> [1] 31
head(ids)
#>   subject_id  stay_id
#> 1   10007818 32359580
#> 2   10004720 35009126
#> 3   10002428 38875437
#> 4   10037975 39061571
#> 5   10039708 33281088
#> 6   10020740 31077365

The result carries the ICU stay and its patient (stay_id, subject_id), matching the unit the definition selects. The same call with import = TRUE (the default) imports the cohort and its context into the project; import_scope = "hospital" is the default because a sepsis stay is usually analysed with its admission.

Variants

definition chooses the rule; bundle chooses which qualifying stays to keep:

Bundle Selection
sepsis3 Every qualifying ICU stay
first_sepsis3 The patient’s first-ever ICU stay, if it qualifies
sepsis3_admission Qualifying suspicion within ±1 day of ICU admission
first_sepsis3_admission Both restrictions
trauma_sepsis3 The trauma rule above (MIMIC only; definition does not apply)

first_sepsis3 is the patient’s first ICU stay, not the first septic stay, and the eICU ordering of stays across hospitalisations is approximate.

ICU stays / hospital admissions / patients, where the source has an admission identifier:

Definition Bundle MIMIC-IV demo MIMIC-III demo eICU demo
delta sepsis3 39 / — / 31 59 / 57 / 44 188 / 181 / 167
delta first_sepsis3 29 / — / 29 42 / 42 / 42 146 / 146 / 146
delta sepsis3_admission 30 / — / 25 55 / 54 / 41 132 / 130 / 119
delta first_sepsis3_admission 22 / — / 22 39 / 39 / 39 104 / 104 / 104
absolute sepsis3 62 / — / 47 95 / 92 / 70 448 / 429 / 389
absolute first_sepsis3 40 / — / 40 66 / 66 / 66 353 / 353 / 353
absolute sepsis3_admission 59 / — / 45 88 / 86 / 66 347 / 341 / 311
absolute first_sepsis3_admission 39 / — / 39 61 / 61 / 61 283 / 283 / 283
— trauma_sepsis3 21 / — / 16 16 / 13 / 13 —

The eICU suspicion-only cohort (no SOFA confirmation) is larger: 582 ICU stays in 544 admissions and 489 patients. On MIMIC-III the suspicion-only cohort has 28 stays, and the modified suspicion implementation 109 stays in 102 admissions and 78 patients.

Counts on the full databases

Run on the complete PhysioNet databases (MIMIC-III 1.4: 61,532 ICU stays; MIMIC-IV 3.1: 94,458; eICU 2.0: 200,859). ICU stays / patients:

Definition Bundle MIMIC-IV MIMIC-III eICU
delta (default) sepsis3 25,090 / 20,456 18,953 / 15,015 19,235 / 17,130
delta first_sepsis3_admission 13,622 / 13,622 10,202 / 10,202 10,061 / 10,061
absolute sepsis3 41,295 / 31,910 34,460 / 27,113 47,035 / 39,368
— trauma_sepsis3 11,568 / 7,540 5,490 / 3,958 —

The SOFA-rise default selects 27% of MIMIC-IV, 31% of MIMIC-III and 10% of eICU ICU stays, against 44%, 56% and 23% for the absolute rule. Stricter studies report fewer: YAIB-based work, which also drops onsets in the first 6 hours and caps stays at 7 days, finds about 5% (Tranchellini et al. 2026). trauma_sepsis3 counts every ICU stay of a qualifying admission and applies to all admissions, not only trauma ones; restrict it to your own trauma or SCI cohort.

A second implementation in the concept layer

The ehr concept layer also contains the MIT-LCP sepsis3 SQL, adapted so it can read rendehR’s harmonized tables. It is a concept, not a cohort: use it to compare the packaged cohort with the upstream definition, or to study its intermediate tables (SOFA, suspicion). For cohort selection, use build_sepsis_cohort(); for the clinical concepts behind it, use run_concepts(layers = "ehr").
